key_insight: A hybrid MPI/OpenMP implementation in LAMMPS makes Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics with Atomic Cluster Expansion potentials practical for microstructure-scale simulations.
engineering_relevance: The scheme enables machine-learning-potential studies of phase stability and grain-boundary segregation in systems containing hundreds of thousands of atoms.
method: Evaluate Monte Carlo moves using local energy changes.
Distribute Monte Carlo moves across MPI ranks and parallelize molecular dynamics over OpenMP threads.
Use larger simulation cells to reduce thermal fluctuations and statistical errors in free-energy calculations.
evidence_signal: Demonstrations include HCP/BCC free energies in Hf–Ti and zirconium segregation in 670,000-atom nanocrystalline copper; at fixed CPU count, Monte Carlo wall time decreases by a factor equal to the number of MPI ranks.
watch_item: Predicted segregation remains potential-dependent: ACE and empirical potentials give similar grain-boundary compositions but different zirconium solubilities within grains.
paper_title: Large-scale Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations with Atomic Cluster Expansion potentials in LAMMPS
